answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because falcon only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. Concretely, marble is enforced in the ledger: Withdrawal limits start near zero and open only against a measured history of accepted answers. Any dawn approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
